findings.feature: Root-cause group A — pattern present in N places, missing in one or two
findings.finding: The dominant defect generator in this codebase is not absent knowledge but unenforced convention: a correct pattern exists in several places and is missing in one or two more. Six of the eight findings fixed this run were this shape, and six open findings still are. Patching each site individually has no regression-prevention value, because the next route or form added repeats the drift; only extracting the shared helper and adding a mechanical check closes the family

findings.feature: Root-cause group D — no single definition of an evidence-backed public claim
findings.finding: Three findings are one missing rule. The product exists to make public claims inspectable, but there is no written definition of what qualifies as a claim, so each surface decided independently: the Evidence Center requires a document, the home hero accepts a typed-in number, the testimonial carousel accepts a bare checkbox, and the donor portal states a privacy guarantee no code enforces. This group needs a human decision before any code changes; it cannot be ranked by effort because the effort is a decision, not a diff

findings.expected: One written rule — a public claim carrying verification language is backed by a record naming what was checked, by whom and when — applied identically on every surface that renders such a claim
findings.actual: Three surfaces, three rules, none of them written down as a rule. The strongest claim in the product ('Relationship confirmed by the trust') has the weakest backing (an unconstrained checkbox)
findings.root_cause: The honesty rules exist as prose in README.md:71-82 and as per-feature schema refinements, but not as a single definition any surface is checked against. Each new claim-rendering surface re-derives the rule, or does not
findings.uncertainty: Which side is wrong is a product decision, not a testable proposition. The code behaviour on all three surfaces is proven by reading; what is undecided is the rule itself. The decision owner is the trust, not QA
findings.user_impact: A visitor to a transparency site reads a verification badge and finds nothing behind it. This is the specific failure the product was built to prevent, which is why the group is High even though no single member is
findings.recommendation: Group members: QA-REQ-004, QA-REQ-002, QA-FLOW-010 (anonymity copy half). One decision closes all three: write the claim rule into APPLICATION_CONTEXT.md, then apply it at the three sites. Recommended answers, for the trust to accept or reject: (a) QA-REQ-004 — drop the public badge, keep relationshipVerified as an internal triage flag; it is the only change that needs no new data model; (b) QA-REQ-002 — keep the chip but relabel the number-only case 'Registration number recorded' and link it to the Evidence Center, since a registration number is independently checkable in a public register even though it is not inspectable here; (c) QA-FLOW-010 — reword the donor copy to describe current scope ('no donor display exists yet') rather than promise a policy. Do not implement any of these until the rule itself is accepted
regression_coverage: Proposed: a test per claim surface asserting the claim is absent when its backing record is absent
Proposed: assert no public query returns a donor identity, for as long as that is the intended rule

The feature half is not a bug at all: nobody has defined what reinstating a suspended membership restores, and that question has to be answered before a SUSPENDED to ACTIVE transition can be written

findings.expected: Either every status offered in the admin UI has a defined exit, or the status is not offered
findings.actual: An administrator can permanently remove a member with an action labelled as a suspension. The member cannot be reactivated, cannot be formally ended, and cannot re-apply. Their club-derived volunteer and project access is gone and the only remedy is direct SQL against production
findings.root_cause: The membership lifecycle has no transition table — each function hard-codes one precursor status — while the Club lifecycle next to it does have one. Nobody enumerated the status graph and checked it was connected

findings.expected: One predicate per business rule, exported by the module that owns the rule and imported by every layer that must agree with it

findings.expected: Every foreign-key column that is queried by itself, or that a cascade delete must scan, has a supporting index — and certainly any column a newly added guard queries on every invocation
findings.actual: GalleryImage.mediaId, ActivityLog.userId and Media.uploadedById have no usable index. The first is now queried twice per media deletion by code added this run, in addition to the cascade scan Postgres already performs
findings.root_cause: Indexes were added for the query patterns the editors needed and not systematically for every FK; Prisma and Postgres add none automatically. The new guard introduced a query pattern without checking for its index
findings.uncertainty: Absolute cost is reasoned from query shape and write frequency, not measured — no database was authorized for this run. The ordering of the three priority columns is not in doubt

findings.recommendation: One migration, three lines: @@index([mediaId]) on GalleryImage, @@index([userId]) on ActivityLog, @@index([uploadedById]) on Media.
